title: Part Six: Popes, Curia and the Myth of Hidden Popes

sections.brief: Who decides in law (cann. 331, 333, 349, 360); how a pope is chosen (Universi Dominici Gregis, vacancy rules, the 7-8 May 2025 conclave, Leo XIV's career; 119 electors and no new cardinals as of May 2026); the Curia under Praedicate Evangelium (19 Mar 2022, in force 5 Jun 2022: Secretariat of State, 16 dicasteries, pope heads Evangelization, five-year terms, offices cease at vacancy); money offices (2020 transfer to APSA, Secretariat for the Economy); office holders as of October 2026; a bishop's appointment as a worked example. Figures: fig-compare (office holders Oct 2026), fig-flow (how a decision moves)

The 'Black Pope' nickname (black cassock; Roman in-joke; anti-Jesuit conspiracy tradition per SPLC, incl. 'Jewish and Masonic proxies'); what the Superior General controls (General Congregation, life term, one order, fourth vow under the pope, no curial post); conflicts 1773 (suppression, Ricci dies a prisoner) and 1981 (Dezza); Arturo Sosa in office as of October 2026, no GC37 found. Figures: fig-compare (claim vs record)

The white/black/grey scheme as a named claim; documented colour nicknames (white, black, red: Propaganda Fide prefect, since 2022 the pope himself) vs éminence grise (Père Joseph); the claim chain (2024 bullion-dealer page, undated pages with conflicting holders; Orsini court title ended 1958/1968; Rothschild trope named as antisemitic); grade: myth; who really decides, with the pope's documented acts against the Jesuits, the Orsini and the Secretariat of State and the real limits. Figures: fig-compare (claim vs record)
